dedupe_keys.name: sustainability assessment of 4g and 5g universal mobile broadband strategies ex ante sdg 9

description: This paper evaluates the future sustainability impacts of delivering universal mobile broadband with either 4G or 5G, quantifying the carbon and other environmental emissions of each strategy. It notes that broadband networks have received less attention than energy or transport (roughly a third of global emissions each) because their footprint is smaller, about 1.8 to 3.9 percent of global emissions, but many countries plan universal mobile broadband over the next decade to meet Sustainable Development Goal 9. The authors state it is the first ex ante sustainability assessment of global universal mobile broadband strategies aimed at SDG Goal 9. Producer: Edward Oughton, Jeongjin Oh, Sara Ballan and Julius Kusuma, submitted to arXiv on 9 November 2023 (statistics, applications). Coverage: global, by strategy, not by named country. Access: free PDF on arXiv. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: the abstract gives no numerical emissions results, and the assessment relies on modelled deployments and emission factors documented in the paper. Simulation uses: a reference for embedding environmental emissions in telecom capacity-planning and deployment-strategy models. Related record: the India 5G universal broadband techno-economic model (model-india5g-universal-broadband-techno-economic), from the same research area.
